subject: DPA annex: transient egress notice, geo-telemetry tags & subprocessor visibility
messages:
From: Sophie Tan <sophie.tan@borealishealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Lam <brian.lam@borealishealth.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Borealis DPA annex: transient egress notice, geo-telemetry tags & subprocessor visibility

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. We are preparing a DPA annex for our legal and security teams and have a couple of operational asks we need Redwood to confirm before we proceed: 

1) Transient cross-region processing: We need an explicit commitment on the maximum window during which customer data may be routed or replicated outside the contracted region (US/EU/APAC). Our baseline ask is a hard ceiling of 72 hours for any temporary replication or crosshop for customer traffic, with an SLA for notification if the window will be exceeded. 

2) Telemetry granularity: For auditability, we require token- or request-level telemetry that includes a region tag and a replication flag so we can prove where processing occurred for specific requests for up to 12 months.

3) Subprocessor visibility: Please provide a snapshot of subprocessors that may see ephemeral cache copies or short-lived replicas (edge caches, analytics providers, and CDN caches). A CSV roster plus the categorization (analytics/cache/infra) would be ideal.

4) Egress spike notice: If cross-region routing will cause >5% of a customer’s monthly token volume to leave the region within any 24h window, we need 24h prior notice and the right to opt out of that burst.

Attached is a one-page annex draft (Borealis_DPA_Annex_Request_20250719.pdf) with the language we prefer — legal will use it as a starting point. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these items as-is or propose alternative operational mitigations?

Appreciate a reply by end of week — our SOC team is standing by.

Best,

Sophie Tan
Data Protection Officer
Borealis Health

Sophie —

Thank you for the clear list and the draft annex. Looping in Marissa (Account Lead), Karthik (Infrastructure/Ops) and Markus (Legal) so we can respond with operational detail and a proposed redline. High level: we can meet most of these asks but want to clarify exact SLAs and telemetry retention to avoid ambig.

Quick notes: 
- Transient window: Ops prefers a 48-hour standard with an approvable escalation to 120 hours for emergency scenarios (force majeure / region outage). We can diagram escalation & approval paths if that’s acceptable to you, but we are prepared to commit to a 72-hour cap in the DPA annex if Borealis needs that as a hard ceiling.

- Telemetry: We can emit per-request region tags and a replication flag to your audit logs. Default retention is 12 months; extended retention can be added as an add-on. We’ll provide sample log schema.

- Subprocessors: attaching current snapshot CSV and an ops playbook. Note some entries are shared infra (cloud provider edge) — we’ll mark which ones may handle ephemeral caches vs. persistent storage.

- Egress spike: We agree to a 24h notice for planned rerouting or capacity-driven migrations. For automatic failover due to outages, we can provide post-event forensic logs and an emergency notification channel; we’d like a carve-out for immediate failover to satisfy availability SLAs.

We’ll draft a proposed redline to the annex and send counters within 24 business hours. Markus — can you take point on the language around the emergency exception and the opt-out mechanics? Karthik — can you provide the log schema and the ops playbook excerpt for inclusion? Marissa — I’ll coordinate with Sophie on timelines.

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Borealis DPA annex: transient egress notice, geo-telemetry tags & subprocessor visibility

Sophie / team —

Technical breakdown below (TL;DR: feasible; some behavioral constraints):

1) Transient replication ceiling: Our platform supports a configurable transient-replication-time-to-live (TTL) for ephemeral copies. Default behavior: 48h TTL. We can set a customer-specific hard TTL at 72h in the control-plane policy for Borealis. For emergency failovers (region outage), we have a documented escalation flow:
   - Automatic failover to nearest region (0–2h) to preserve availability.
   - Ops performs a snapshot and flags data with replication_flag=true in logs.
   - Post-event: we initiate asynchronous cleanup (garbage-collect ephemeral cache) and have an automated job to assert deletion within 120h; audit evidence is published to the customer feed.

2) Telemetry schema (sample):
   - timestamp_iso, request_id, model_id, customer_id, region_origin, region_processed, replication_flag, bytes_processed, latency_ms, instance_id
   - We will provide CSV/JSON samples and a queryable feed (read-only) to your DPO with 12 months retention.

3) Subprocessors & caches: The attached CSV differentiates categories: EDGE_CACHE (may hold ephemeral segments), ANALYTICS (pseudonymized telemetry only), and INFRA (cloud provider managed). For ephemeral cache entries we only persist opaque keys — not raw payloads — unless the customer has specifically opted into cache persistence.

4) Egress spike rule: We can surface pre-scheduled maintenance and planned capacity shifts 24h in advance. For automatic failovers that cause spikes, we will notify as soon as the event is detected and provide forensic telemetry. For the opt-out: if Borealis chooses to opt out of an upcoming planned cross-region burst, the request needs to be raised 24h prior to the maintenance window — we cannot apply opt-out retroactively to emergency failovers.

Next steps: I’ll attach the log-schema examples and an ops playbook excerpt to this thread. Marissa — can you confirm whether we should commit to a 72h hard TTL in the annex or keep 48h default + 72h hard ceiling?

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sophie —

I reviewed your annex and Karthik’s technical response. I’m attaching a redline we can propose back to Borealis (DocuSign-ready). Key legal positions: 

- We will accept a DPA clause that sets a 72-hour hard ceiling for transient replication, with a defined emergency carve-out limited to declared region outages; any emergency extension beyond 72h requires written consent from Borealis or escalation per the annex approval flow.

- Telemetry: Redwood will provide the per-request telemetry feed with 12 months retention. Any additional retention beyond 12 months will be on a paid addendum.

- Subprocessors: Redwood will deliver a quarterly snapshot and a one-time roster on onboarding; for anything that could see ephemeral caches we will highlight categories (EDGE_CACHE/ANALYTICS/INFRA). Sixty (60) days notice will be provided for adding a new subprocessor in the EDGE_CACHE category unless the addition is required for critical security/availability reasons — in that case we will provide expedited notice and remediation options.

- Egress spike opt-out: We will include the 24h planned-notice promise for maintenance-driven routing changes and a post-event forensic packet for emergency failover. Retroactive opt-outs are not feasible for emergency failovers.

If Borealis agrees in principle we will publish the redline to the shared Drive and send a DocuSign envelope for the annex. Sophie — please confirm if the emergency carve-out language below is acceptable and we’ll route to sign.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
